question: The amount on a sum of ₹6000 at 5% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years, will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective CI rate for 2 years = R + R + (R × R)/100

⇒ Effective Rate = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = 10.25%

Amount percentage = 100% (Principal) + 10.25% (Interest) = 110.25%

⇒ Amount = 110.25% of 6000 = (110.25 ÷ 100) × 6000 = 6615

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6615.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• P = ₹6000 Start ₹6300 1 Year A = ₹6615 2 Years 
 
 + 5% 
 
 + 5% Compound Interest (5% p.a.) 

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹6000

Rate (R) = 5% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 6000 × (1 + 5/100)²

⇒ A = 6000 × (1 + 1/20)²

⇒ A = 6000 × (21/20) × (21/20)

⇒ A = 6000 × (441 / 400)

⇒ A = 15 × 441

⇒ A = 6615

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6615.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Compound Interest Rate

For 2 years at R%, effective rate = 2R + (R²/100)%. This helps compute total CI directly without using the standard compound interest formula.

Difference Between CI and SI

For exactly 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a sum is calculated as Difference = P × (R/100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes halved (R/2) and the number of compounding periods becomes doubled (2n).
